data.why: A backyard swimming pool in the yard setting, dug into the cut, built up the way a real one is: a hole that drains away, a concrete shell, a blue liner, then water, then a pump and pipes. The camera opens close on the dig, follows the pit as it drains and cracks, then pulls out to the pump loop, the algae, the storm overflow and the finish with edge rocks, steps and a light. Counters show the 8-hour turnover and the 2,500 gallons an hour, and the myth is shown by taking the water away so the blue liner is left.

ideas.idea: dig a hole in the yard and pour water into it, and you think you have a pool
the thirsty soil drinks all 20,000 gallons and the hole drains dry
the pit is left empty and the wet dirt slumps off its walls
soaked soil is heavy, so the walls of the hole crack
pour a concrete floor and walls to hold the dirt back
concrete drinks water too, so a blue liner goes over it
fill the sealed shell and the water finally stays
still water goes bad, so a pump and pipes keep it moving
a lined, filled and sealed hole is a swimming pool
the pump and pipes together are a filtration system
water leaves through a drain, passes the filter and returns clean through a jet
every drop makes a full trip through the filter about once every eight hours
so the pump pushes about 2,500 gallons an hour through one pipe
the sun warms the water, algae grows and the pool turns green
a storm adds rain, the green pool overflows over the lawn
chlorine clears the algae and a drain carries the extra water away
everyone thinks pool water is blue, so we take the water away to leave only the liner
water absorbs red light and the blue liner does the rest
add rocks round the edge, steps into the water and a light
a calm, clear, finished swimming pool

chain.shows: the filled hole drains dry into the soil
chain.stakes: 20,000 gallons of water are lost and the yard is left a muddy pit

chain.shows: the warm, still water turns green with algae
a storm dumps rain and the green pool spills across the lawn
chain.stakes: the lawn floods and the algae spreads to the whole yard

surprises.claim: A pool pump should turn over all of the pool water about once every 8 hours
Free chlorine in a pool should stay at about 1 to 3 parts per million
